subsystems.name: Token embedding and routing input
subsystems.role: turns each input token into a vector the router can score.

subsystems.name: Gating network (router)
subsystems.role: computes a score for each expert per token and selects the top few.

subsystems.name: Expert networks
subsystems.role: independent sub-networks that process only the tokens assigned to them.

subsystems.name: Dispatch and combine module
subsystems.role: sends tokens to chosen experts and merges their outputs with gate weights.

subsystems.name: Load balancing controller
subsystems.role: keeps experts evenly used so none are idle or overloaded.

subsystems.name: Distributed execution engine
subsystems.role: runs experts in parallel across many accelerators.

buildSteps.title: Choose the MoE configuration
buildSteps.detail: Decide the number of experts, how many are active per token (top-k), and the size of each expert. Common choices are 8 to 64 experts with top-2 routing.

buildSteps.title: Initialize experts and router
buildSteps.detail: Create the expert feed-forward networks with random weights and initialize the router's linear layer.

buildSteps.title: Implement routing logic
buildSteps.detail: For each token, compute gate logits, apply softmax to get expert probabilities, and select the highest-scoring k experts.

buildSteps.title: Add load balancing
buildSteps.detail: Introduce an auxiliary loss that penalizes uneven expert usage, and set a capacity factor to limit how many tokens any one expert can receive per batch.

buildSteps.title: Set up distributed execution
buildSteps.detail: Partition experts across devices and implement all-to-all communication so tokens are sent to the devices holding their chosen experts.

buildSteps.title: Train the model
buildSteps.detail: In the forward pass, route tokens, let experts process them, combine outputs weighted by gate values, and backpropagate gradients to both experts and the router.

buildSteps.title: Optimize inference
buildSteps.detail: Reduce latency with batching, caching, and overlapping communication with computation; possibly specialize kernels for sparse expert activation.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and serve
buildSteps.detail: Integrate the trained MoE into a serving system with expert parallelism, monitor load balance and output quality, and adjust routing as needed.

prerequisites.why: MoE layers replace or augment standard transformer feed-forward blocks, so the base architecture and training loops must already work.
Models with many experts and billions of parameters require frameworks that can shard parameters and synchronize gradients across devices.
All-to-all communication between experts is bandwidth-intensive and can become the bottleneck without fast links such as NVLink or InfiniBand.
Basic auxiliary losses and capacity limits exist, but stable and efficient routing that avoids expert collapse is still an active research area.
Frameworks support MoE, but highly optimized kernels for dynamic token routing and sparse expert execution are still maturing.

pathway.milestone: sparse MoE models with top-1 or top-2 routing, such as Switch Transformer (2021) and Mixtral 8x7B (2023), deployed in production
pathway.unlocks: larger models at lower inference cost, because only a fraction of parameters run per token.

pathway.milestone: improved routing algorithms like expert choice (where experts select tokens) and soft routing reduce load imbalance and training instability
pathway.unlocks: more reliable scaling to trillions of parameters and better utilization of all experts.

pathway.milestone: hardware and software co-design: chips with fast on-chip networks and MoE-aware compilers
pathway.unlocks: lower communication overhead and higher effective compute throughput.

pathway.milestone: conditional computation throughout the model, with routing at every layer and dynamic expert specialization
pathway.unlocks: modular, efficient AI that activates only relevant parameters for each input.
